note: Files this fork deletes that upstream still owns. Every one is a modify/delete conflict on the next sync, so each is asserted here rather than rediscovered: the resolver prints the entry and can apply it. LOCAL-PATCHES.md and local/sync/convergence-ledger.md stay the evidence; this file is the machine-readable claim. Generated from `git diff <base>..HEAD --diff-filter=D`, NOT from the log: a merge resolution can delete a file without a commit of its own, which is how agent-dashboard-open-mode.ts was missed the first time. A path listed as deleted must be absent at HEAD and present at upstream/main, and conflicts.mjs reports a stale entry on read. Statuses were settled on 2026-10-26: the fork ships the Agent Dashboard as a content-area view and rejects upstream’s drawer/pop-out delivery, so the renderer half is a recorded product deletion and only the mutually inert main-process pair is held. Each entry records `upstreamBlob`, the upstream version of the file the decision was judged against — read at the upstream base of the merge that settled it (`f173998203` for the 2026-10-28 sync), not at today's `upstream/main`: when upstream's blob for that path changes the entry reverts to `pending-decision` instead of keeping a `git rm -f` proposal written about a file that no longer exists in that form, and binding against a moved upstream would approve changes nobody reviewed. An entry present on neither side is reported as prunable, and an entry with no blob at all is reported as unbound.

statuses.expected-deletion: settled: the deletion is the fork's answer and a sync re-applies it
statuses.pending-decision: not settled: the deletion exists but nobody has chosen between restoring and keeping it
statuses.restore: settled the other way: the file comes back and a sync must not re-delete it
